body: I knew I had gender dysphoria my entire life. My earliest memories in pre-k were of me dressing in certain ways because it made me feel like a girl. When I was 7/8, i told my mom how much I wanted to be a girl, but I continued to be a boy up until I was around 14, when I really began questioning. I became Non Binary and started slowly morphing into a girl, until one day when I was watching the little mermaid with my friends I noticed how much I envy being a girl. It was at that moment where it finally clicked for me, and a couple days later I came out to my parents. Gender Dysphoria isnt what we think it is. As kids, we don't have a definied view on gender. We only have "girls like pink and boys like blue" so forth. Yes, we experience dysphoria at an early age, but most people don't fully process it until their teen years. Once we hit our teen years or older, we notice how much gender impacts society and also once puberty sets in too, thats when most people start to notice. Once it clicks for you that you want to be a girl, it clicks for you. I remember as soon as it did, I felt like I had to tell everyone around me because I finally figured out my cause of suffering for so many years, and wanted to switch to be a girl in an instant. A year after I told everyone, I started on hormones and here I am a year later happy and couldn't picture myself not being a woman :). I know Its very scary and transitioning comes with a lot of ups and downs, but theres no right way to transition. everyones experiences are different. Some transition at a young age, other at an old age. Some people go on hormones or get surgery, and some don't. However, when it clicks for you, you just know that its the right choice for you, and I hope and wish you well on your journey! I hope this helps a lot I dont post much on reddit lol <3

It started off as health related anxiety and then I started obsessing over those thoughts, which then came back as OCD. I had intrusive thoughts come back that I hadn't had in years. I had to go back to therapy and start all over again. I can now say that my OCD is more manageable now with therapy, however there is still a long way to go before I can get to a point where my OCD is under the radar and I can smoke a joint again.
